title: TrustLock: a dead man's switch for SOL
summary: Lock SOL for a beneficiary. Check in to keep it; miss the deadline and they can claim it. The program enforces the deadline with the on-chain clock.
what: TrustLock locks SOL in an escrow account for a beneficiary you choose, with a deadline. While the deadline is in the future you can **check in** to push it later, or **cancel** and take your SOL back. If you stop checking in and the deadline passes, the beneficiary can **claim** everything. The website never decides who gets paid: the program reads the Solana clock on every call and refuses anything that breaks the rules.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js 14 app, unchanged apart from the base path, static export and the program ID. The program was built from `switch/` at this commit and deployed fresh to devnet.

try_steps.see: Two transactions: `initialize` (creates the escrow) then `deposit` (moves 0.1 SOL into it). The toast says "Escrow created successfully." and a card shows Balance 0.10 SOL, a deadline 15 seconds away and an Active badge.

diagram:
Owner (Account 1)
  │ initialize(deadline, beneficiary, seed)   creates ─▶ Escrow PDA  seeds = ["escrow", owner, seed]
  │ deposit(amount)                           SOL ─────▶   owner | beneficiary | deadline | last_checkin | bump | seed
  │ checkin(new_deadline)   only while now <  deadline       lamports = deposited SOL + rent
  │ cancel()                any time, by the owner ──▶ all lamports back to owner, account closed
Beneficiary (Account 2)
    claim()                 only when now >= deadline ─▶ all lamports to beneficiary, account closed
accounts: PDA of this program, seeds `["escrow", owner, seed]`
owner, beneficiary, deadline, last_checkin, bump, seed, **and the locked SOL itself** as the account's lamports
Pays rent and the deposit; the only one who can deposit, check in or cancel
Any address, stored in the escrow

instructions.name: `initialize`: create the escrow
steps: `init, payer = owner` creates a new account owned by the program at the PDA `["escrow", owner, seed]`. The owner pays its rent.
`space = 93 + seed.len()`: 8 (Anchor discriminator) + 32 (owner) + 32 (beneficiary) + 8 (deadline) + 8 (last_checkin) + 1 (bump) + 4 (string length prefix) = 93, plus the seed bytes.
`require!(deadline > Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp, ...)` rejects a deadline in the past with `InvalidDeadline`.
It stores owner, beneficiary, deadline, the current time as `last_checkin`, the PDA bump and the seed, so later instructions can re-derive the address.

instructions.name: `deposit`: put SOL into the escrow
steps: `require!(amount > 0, ...)` rejects an empty deposit with `InvalidAmount`.
It calls the System Program's `transfer` from the owner's wallet to the escrow PDA. The owner signs the transaction, so the transfer is authorised.
The account constraints re-derive the PDA from the stored seed and bump and check `escrow.owner == owner`, so you can only fund your own escrow through this instruction.

instructions.name: `checkin`: prove you are alive and move the deadline
steps: `now < escrow.deadline` or it fails with `DeadlineExceeded`: once the deadline passes, the money belongs to the beneficiary's claim.
`new_deadline > now` or `InvalidDeadline`.
It writes the new deadline and sets `last_checkin = now`. The constraint `escrow.owner == owner.key()` means only the owner can check in.

instructions.name: `claim`: the beneficiary takes everything after the deadline
steps: `Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp >= deadline` or it fails with `DeadlineNotReached`.
It reads the escrow's full lamport balance, sets it to 0 and adds it to the beneficiary. The program can do this directly because it owns the escrow account.
`constraint = escrow.beneficiary == beneficiary.key()` means the money can only go to the stored beneficiary, and `close = beneficiary` closes the account.

instructions.name: `cancel`: the owner takes everything back
steps: Same lamport move as `claim`, but to the owner, with no time check: the owner can cancel at any time, even after the deadline if the beneficiary has not claimed yet.
`escrow.owner == owner.key()` plus the owner's signature mean nobody else can cancel.

innovation.title: the clock is the referee, and the PDA is the vault
innovation.text: There is no off-chain timer and no keeper. Each instruction asks the runtime for the current time with `Clock::get()` and compares it with the stored deadline, so the same transaction is allowed or refused depending only on when it lands. And the SOL is not held in a separate token account or a wallet with a private key: it sits in the escrow PDA's own lamports, so the program can pay it out by editing lamports directly.

refs.note: checkin and claim are mirror images around the same deadline

more: The `seed` is chosen by the client (the app uses the current time in milliseconds), so one owner can run many switches, each at its own address.

Read the `Claim` accounts closely: in the program, `beneficiary` is an `AccountInfo`, not a `Signer`. After the deadline, anyone could send `claim`, but the money can still only go to the stored beneficiary. The app's bundled IDL marks the beneficiary as a signer, so in the app the beneficiary claims from their own wallet. Exercise 5 asks you to make the program enforce that too.

frontend.title: Connect: an Anchor `Program` from the wallet
steps: When the wallet connects, the app wraps it in an `AnchorProvider` and builds `new Program(IDL, PROGRAM_ID, provider)`. Every button below calls `program.methods.<instruction>(...)` on it.

frontend.title: Create: derive the PDA, then send `initialize` and `deposit`
steps: The deadline is computed from the **chain's** block time (`getBlockTime`), not the browser clock, so it matches what `Clock::get()` will see.
`seed = new Date().getTime().toString()`, then `findProgramAddressSync(["escrow", publicKey, seed])` gives the same address the program derives.
Two separate `.rpc()` calls: that is why the app asks you to approve two transactions.

frontend.title: List: find your escrows with `memcmp` filters
steps: `program.account.escrow.all([...memcmp...])` asks the RPC for every escrow account whose bytes match at an offset.
Offset 8 is right after the 8-byte discriminator, where `owner` is stored; offset 8 + 32 = 40 is `beneficiary`. That is how the beneficiary sees escrows they did not create.

frontend.title: Check in, cancel, claim
steps: `checkin` sends `currentTime + extension` as the new deadline, again using chain time.
`cancel` and `claim` pass just the escrow (and the beneficiary for claim); Anchor checks the rest against the account constraints you saw above.

frontend.title: The UI guard in front of the program guard
steps: The Claim button refuses to send before the deadline ("Cannot claim yet"). That is a convenience only: the real rule is `DeadlineNotReached` in the program, which our test script hit directly (see Proof).

exercises.title: Find the PDA yourself
steps: Create a 15s escrow in the app.

In a Node script with `@solana/web3.js`, call `PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync` with seeds `["escrow", <your address>, <seed>]` and program `6km4NhrxLPcMTXVmZyKsBBsmmoqXHu1NT6P5uFL5FFjP`. Get the seed from the escrow account on Explorer (it is the last field) or from the `initialize` instruction data.
Compare with the escrow address in the `initialize` transaction on Explorer.
exercises.expect: The derived address is exactly the escrow account the app created.
exercises.hint: The third seed is the `seed` argument the app chose — a 13-digit millisecond timestamp, as a string, not as a number.
exercises.approach: Read the seed from the `initialize` instruction data or the escrow account, then `findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('escrow'), owner.toBuffer(), Buffer.from(seed)], programId)`. It must equal the escrow address in that transaction.

exercises.title: Check the account size
steps: Open your escrow address on Solana Explorer (devnet).
Read its data size.
exercises.expect: 93 + the length of the seed. The app's seed is a 13-digit millisecond timestamp, so 106 bytes.
exercises.hint: Anchor's 8-byte discriminator is included. The seed is a string, so it carries a 4-byte length prefix plus the bytes.
exercises.approach: On Explorer the data length is 93 + seed.len(). For a 13-digit seed that's 106. If you change the seed length, the size (and the rent) will change with it.

exercises.title: See the two guards
steps: Create a **30s** escrow to Account 2.
Immediately switch to Account 2 and press Claim.
exercises.expect: The app shows "Cannot claim yet" and sends nothing (the UI guard). The program-level refusal, `DeadlineNotReached`, is in the Proof section from the script that bypasses the UI.
exercises.hint: Claim and check-in both read `Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp` and compare it to the stored deadline. The two instructions just disagree about which side of the deadline is allowed.
exercises.approach: On a 30-second escrow, claim immediately as the beneficiary (should fail: deadline not reached) and check in as the owner after it expires (should fail: DeadlineExceeded, error 6002). After expiry, Claim as the beneficiary should succeed, as in the recorded run.

exercises.title: Follow the money in a claim
steps: Open the claim transaction `5xVrtsfr…` from the Proof section.
Look at the balance changes.
exercises.expect: The beneficiary gains 0.02118872 SOL: the 0.02 SOL deposit plus the escrow's rent, because `claim` moves every lamport and closes the account.
exercises.hint: `close = beneficiary` (or whichever destination the instruction uses) adds the account's remaining lamports — the rent — to the claim amount.
exercises.approach: Note the beneficiary's balance before Claim, then after. The increase is the deposited SOL plus the escrow's rent, minus the transaction fee. The escrow account should disappear (no longer exists on Explorer).

exercises.title: Make the beneficiary sign
steps: Clone the fork at the pinned commit and open `switch/programs/switch/src/lib.rs`.
In `Claim`, change `pub beneficiary: AccountInfo<'info>` to `pub beneficiary: Signer<'info>` (and drop the `/// CHECK` comment).
Run `anchor build` and `anchor test` with a test that sends `claim` signed only by a third wallet.
exercises.expect: That claim now fails with a missing-signature error; a claim signed by the beneficiary still succeeds after the deadline.
exercises.hint: Today the beneficiary does not sign `claim`: anyone who spots an expired escrow can submit the instruction and the funds still go to the stored beneficiary. Making them sign is a product choice.
exercises.approach: Add `beneficiary: Signer` and `has_one = beneficiary` on the escrow. A third wallet's claim should then fail a constraint, while the beneficiary's claim still works. Decide whether that's the behaviour you want (it stops a stranger paying the fee to help the beneficiary).

not_covered: Create (initialize + deposit), Cancel, the beneficiary's Claim and the expired Check In rejection were all clicked through in the hosted app. A successful Check In and a date-picked escrow were verified by script only.
objectives: Use the Clock sysvar to enforce a deadline the frontend cannot override.
Follow SOL into an escrow PDA and back out, and see `close` return the rent to a chosen wallet.
Tell the two guards apart: the beneficiary cannot claim early, and the owner cannot check in after the deadline.
prereqs: Two Phantom accounts (owner and beneficiary) and about 0.2 devnet SOL in the owner's.
[PulseFund](/lessons/pulsefund-sol/) (SOL into a PDA, rent) and [Picassol](/lessons/picassol-hackathon/) (PDAs from seeds).

build.note: The program is in `switch/`. The app is a Next.js 14 frontend at the repo root.
